library(magrittr)
library(driveanalytics)

knitr::opts_knit$set(echo = FALSE)

# Get the render format
render_format <- knitr::opts_knit$get('rmarkdown.pandoc.to')

## Overview
This method plots timeseries trends for a value-based datatype. It can be used to visualise how a specific clinical metric (e.g., a lab test value) changes either with age or since a specific event.

## Method

1. The timeseries trend is created using [GAM](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/mgcv/html/gam.html)

## Considerations and Limitations
* The trend line is fitted arbitrarily and should be checked to ensure it is meaningful
* Therefore, this method is deprecated now as the timeseries analysis can be better done with the GAMLSS module which has greater flexibility over parameter selection for the fit

## Example

This example shows how a randomly generated set of values change over time and can be plotted and fit.

The output shows:

1. The values for metric X, in cohort A, increase linearly from approximately 4.0 at birth, to approximately 7.5
1. The values for metric X, in cohort B, are static for all ages at approximately 3.0
1. The values for metric Y, in cohort A, are static for all ages at approximately 6.0
1. The values for metrix Y, in cohory B, decrease linearly from approximately 6.0 at birth to approximately 3.0

```{r, example, echo=FALSE, dpi=200, out.width="100%", fig.dim = c(8, 6)}

# Create a random sample of patients in two cohorts and assign random events
set.seed(123)
n = 500
nev = n * 4
df_pde <- tibble::tibble(
  project_id = 1:n,
  cohort_id = project_id,
  cohort = sample(c("A","B"), n, replace = TRUE),
  birth_date = as.Date("2020-1-1")
)
df_event <- df_pde %>%
  dplyr::sample_n(nev, replace = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::select(-birth_date) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    metric = sample(paste("Metric", c("X","Y")), nev, replace = TRUE),
    taken_datetime = as.Date("2020-1-1") + lubridate::days(sample(1:1004, nev, replace = T)),
    value = dplyr::if_else(
      cohort == "A",
      dplyr::if_else(
        metric == "Metric X",
        as.numeric(taken_datetime - as.Date("2020-1-1")) / 1000 * 3 + 4,
        4
      ),
      dplyr::if_else(
        metric == "Metric X",
        6,
        as.numeric(taken_datetime - as.Date("2020-1-1")) / 1000 * -3 + 6
      )
    ),
    value = value + rnorm(nev)
  )

gta <- gen_timeseries_analysis(
  df_event, df_pde, "metric", "value", "taken_datetime", "cohort",
  hor_axis = "Years since birth", overlay_cohorts = FALSE
)

gta$plt

```
